newsitem.title: UK: NWE spot gasoline steady to firmer on NYMEX lead.
newsitem.headline: NWE spot gasoline steady to firmer on NYMEX lead.

text.p: NWE spot gasoline prices were steady to slightly firmer on Wednesday with barges supported by short covering while bullish U.S. data strengthened NYMEX unleaded futures and underpinned cargo prices, traders said.
Eurograde gasoline barges traded at $194 fob Rotterdam as a German buyer sought cover ahead of an extended weekend.
Later offers were at that level and those for the whole of May at $195 fob with regular $9-10 lower.
Weekly stocks data from the American Petroleum Institute (API) were viewed slightly constructive for the NWE cargo market but some doubts were expressed over the data's validity.
"The data is a bit weird," one futures trader said.

The API figures showed "implied demand" for gasoline at a record 8.76 million barrels per day (bpd), in contrast to recent data from the U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA) which showed year-to-date gasoline demand has been "underwhelming" this year.

Some players were surprised the physical market had not moved higher after bullish U.S. stocks figures. However forward price indicators May swaps saw offers rise a couple of dollars to $196 a tonne fob ARA.

U.S. gasoline stocks fell 3.6 million to 190.5 million barrels last week and were some 13.2 million barrels below last years already low levels. Imports totalled some 473,000 barrels per day. --Colin Wooster, London Newsroom, +44 171 542 7456
